question: According to Census 2011, which state of the following states has the highest population?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the Census 2011, Bihar has a total population of approximately **104 million**, making it one of the most densely populated states in India.
 
• Bihar accounts for about **8.6% of India's total population**, with a population density of 1,106 persons per square kilometer.
 
• The state's population growth rate between 2001 and 2011 was nearly **25.42%**, which is among the highest in the country.
 
• Bihar's population is predominantly rural, with **88.71% of its population living in rural areas** and only 11.29% residing in urban regions.
 
• Bihar has a **sex ratio of 918 females per 1000 males**, which is slightly below the national average of 940 as per Census 2011.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **West Bengal:**

 
 
• West Bengal had a population of approximately **91.3 million** as per Census 2011, making it the fourth most populous state in India.
 
• It has a population density of **1,028 persons per square kilometer**, which is one of the highest densities in the country.
 
• West Bengal's urbanization rate is higher compared to Bihar, with **31.89% of its population living in urban areas**.
 
• The literacy rate of West Bengal stands at **76.26%**, reflecting better educational attainment compared to some other states.
 
 
 
• **Rajasthan:**
 
 
• Rajasthan had a population of approximately **68.5 million** as per Census 2011, making it the seventh most populous state in India.
 
• It is the largest state in India by area but has a comparatively low population density of **200 persons per square kilometer**.
 
• Rajasthan's population is predominantly rural, with **75.12% of its population living in rural areas**.
 
• The sex ratio of Rajasthan is **928 females per 1000 males**, slightly above Bihar's ratio.
 
 
 
• **Tamil Nadu:**
 
 
• Tamil Nadu had a population of approximately **72.1 million** as per Census 2011, ranking sixth in terms of population among Indian states.
 
• It has a population density of **555 persons per square kilometer**, higher than Rajasthan but significantly lower than Bihar.
 
• Tamil Nadu is among the most urbanized states in India, with **48.45% of its population living in urban areas**.
 
• The literacy rate of Tamil Nadu stands at **80.09%**, showcasing advanced educational progress.
